title: A Bold Request at Night
overview: Naomi sends Ruth to ask Boaz, a relative, to marry her and protect the family, and he agrees if a closer relative steps aside.

parts.label: Naomi's plan (vv. 1-5)
parts.note: Naomi wants a secure future for Ruth, which then meant marriage, so she points her to Boaz, a relative who might take on that duty. The threshing floor was where harvested barley was tossed so wind blew away the husks, and workers often celebrated and slept there to guard the grain.

parts.label: Night at the threshing floor (vv. 6-9)
parts.note: Ruth lies at Boaz's feet and asks him to spread the corner of his garment over her, a known way of asking for marriage and protection. She calls him a family redeemer: a close relative expected to rescue relatives in trouble, buy back family land, and care for a dead man's widow.

parts.label: Boaz's answer (vv. 10-13)
parts.note: Boaz praises Ruth for choosing loyalty to her late husband's family over a younger man of her own choosing, and promises to act. But another relative has the first right, so he must give that man the chance first.

parts.label: Leaving before dawn (vv. 14-15)
parts.note: Boaz sends Ruth home early to protect her reputation and loads her shawl with barley; the exact amount is uncertain, but it was generous. Many scholars note the night has a charged, delicate feel, though the text presents both as acting honorably.

parts.label: Waiting for news (vv. 16-18)
parts.note: The gift tells Naomi she will not be left empty, reversing her bitter words when she first came home. Naomi is sure Boaz will settle the matter that same day; how Christians later read the redeemer idea is as a picture of Jesus rescuing people.

disagreement: Christians differ on how to read the night scene itself, some seeing a fully innocent appeal following local custom and others seeing deliberate sexual overtones in a risky, morally complex moment.
think: When have you had to take a real risk to ask someone for help, and what made that person feel safe or unsafe to ask?
